issues.failure_explanation: The proof attributes the specific rate bound sup|h_{n_2}-r_F| <= 1/n_2 to Dini's theorem (eq:Dini-uniform), but Dini's theorem only yields convergence to 0 without any rate. The sandwich {r_F <= epsilon-2/n_2} subset Gamma_{n_2} subset {r_F <= epsilon} derived from this rate is unjustified as written; the left inclusion additionally requires strict inequality sup|h_{n_2}-r_F| < 1/n_2 to cross the strict threshold test in the definition of Gamma_{n_2}, which the stated non-strict bound does not provide.

failure_location.quote:
By \eqref{eq:Dini-uniform} (with this $R$), for all sufficiently large $n_2$ we have
\[
\sup_{|z|\le R}|h_{n_2}(z,F)-r_F(z)|\le \frac1{n_2}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 1/n_2 margin in the sandwich with delta_{n_2} = sup|h_{n_2}-r_F| (which tends to 0 by Dini) and adjust the grid argument with the corrected margins 1/n_2 +/- delta_{n_2}; use a strict margin to handle the boundary of the threshold test h_{n_2} < epsilon - 1/n_2.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of Hausdorff convergence d_H(Gamma_{n_2}(F), sigma_{ap,epsilon}(K_F)) -> 0 via the sandwich and standard grid argument is incomplete as written. The SCI upper bounds in the theorem statement remain correct but their proof has a gap in Step 3(d).
issues.title: Unjustified convergence rate in Dini-based Hausdorff argument
issues.why_classification: Replacing the unjustified rate with the actual convergence error and adjusting the margins is a short, local, routine repair that preserves every substantive claim (SCI upper bounds and Hausdorff convergence) with no new lemma, construction, or reoptimization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
choose $u_m(S)$ to be the $\prec$-least extension $v$ such that
\[
\Sigma(v)\ \subseteq\ S\cap 2^m.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The greedy star-priority construction chooses '*' at each step whenever admissible, but this locally optimal choice can block all extensions at a later level, causing u_m(S) = bottom and k_m(S) = 0. Concretely, let S contain all strings of length <= 2 together with all strings of length >= 3 whose second coordinate is 0 (so S contains S_{A,x} with A = {2} and x = (0,0,...), and A is coinfinite). The greedy construction gives u_2 = ** (both stars admissible at level 2 since S cap 2^2 = 2^2), but no extension of ** is admissible at level 3 (since S cap 2^3 = {tau : tau(2) = 0} contains no cube of dimension 3), so u_3 = bottom and k_m = 0 for all m >= 3. Yet S is in V and |m \ A| -> infinity. Hence the claim k_m(S) >= |m \ A| is false and the forward implication S in V implies z_0 in sigma_ap(K_{F_S}) fails.

failure_location.quote: By the star-priority construction of $u_m(S)$ (it chooses $\ast$ whenever that choice preserves $\Sigma(\cdot)\subseteq S\cap 2^m$), the pattern $u_m(S)$ has at least as many $\ast$-coordinates as any admissible witness pattern.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the encoding of tree complexity into the dynamics F_S so that both directions of S in V iff z_0 in sigma_ap(K_{F_S}) hold, requiring a construction whose approximate-eigenvalue structure detects Silver-tree containment through a consistent (not merely greedy or cardinality-based) mechanism, and re-prove the spectral properties and the main equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: The forward direction of the Silver-Koopman equivalence (eq:SilverApKoopEquiv) is false with the greedy construction, invalidating the spectral equivalence S in V iff z_0 in sigma_ap(K_{F_S}). This breaks the Borel reduction from ill-founded trees to the approximate-eigenvalue decision set (thm:route-IF-to-Az0), the Sigma^1_1-completeness of A_{z_0}, and all SCI lower bounds (SCI_A = infinity at L-infinity via thm:SCI_A_infty_Linfty_decision; SCI_G = infinity via thm:SCI_G_infty_mclasses and cor:SCI_G_infty_alpha). The 1-Lipschitz variant (def:Psi-Lip) uses the same u_m(S) and is equally affected. The headline claims of the paper at the L-infinity endpoint are not established.
issues.title: Greedy star-priority construction fails to detect Silver trees
issues.why_classification: The greedy star-priority claim is not merely unproved but false, and no comparable version of the forward implication survives with the current construction. Fixing both directions of the equivalence while preserving the reverse direction requires essentially new encoding of tree consistency (not just star-counts) into the spectral structure of F_S, together with new proofs of the spectral lemmas and the equivalence. No complete source-supported repair is available.
